• Countries like **Russia** have state-of-the-art facilities to conduct specialized tests such as high-altitude performance and extreme weather trials.
 
• These tests ensure the engine can withstand diverse and challenging operational environments.
 
 
 
• **Indigenous Capability Development:**
 
 
• The KDE initiative aligns with India’s **Make in India** and **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (self-reliant India) missions, aiming to reduce dependency on foreign defense equipment.
 
• Successful certification of the KDE will mark a significant milestone in India’s aerospace sector.

questions.question: Technological innovation was key to the success of the Green Revolution. The success of HYV seeds in India was contingent on which critical input?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chemical fertilisers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Technological innovation** played a pivotal role in the success of the **Green Revolution**, particularly in countries like India. The introduction of **High Yielding Variety (HYV) seeds** significantly boosted agricultural productivity.
 
• The success of HYV seeds was contingent upon the availability of **chemical fertilisers**, as these seeds required higher inputs of nutrients to achieve their full yield potential.
 
• **Chemical fertilisers** provided essential nutrients such as **nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), and potassium (K)** to crops, which are critical for growth and high yields.
 
• India saw a dramatic increase in food grain production during the Green Revolution period (1960s-70s) due to the combined use of **HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers, and advanced irrigation techniques**.
 
• Other inputs like **forest cover, hand tools, and organic compost** were not sufficient to meet the nutrient requirements of HYV seeds, making **chemical fertilisers** indispensable for their success.
 
• *Hence, the correct answer is **Chemical fertilisers**__.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

__
 
• **High Yielding Variety (HYV) Seeds:**

 
 
• HYV seeds were first introduced in India during the **1960s** as part of the Green Revolution.
 
• These seeds were developed to produce more grains per hectare compared to traditional seeds.
 
• They required intensive agricultural inputs such as **chemical fertilisers, pesticides, and regular irrigation** for maximum productivity.
 
• Examples include wheat varieties like **Kalyan Sona** and **Sonora 64**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Chemical Fertilisers:**
 
 
• Fertilisers supply essential nutrients like **nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium**, which are vital for plant growth and development.
 
• The use of chemical fertilisers in India saw a significant increase during the Green Revolution, contributing to the country’s ability to achieve self-sufficiency in food grains.
 
• India became one of the largest producers of food grains globally due to the use of fertilisers.
 
• Popular fertilisers include **urea (nitrogen), DAP (diammonium phosphate), and potash**.
 
 
 
• **Green Revolution in India:**
 
 
• The Green Revolution refers to the period during the **1960s and 1970s** when India achieved rapid agricultural growth by adopting modern farming techniques.
 
• Key aspects included the introduction of HYV seeds, expansion of irrigation facilities, and use of fertilisers and pesticides.
 
• It was spearheaded by **Dr. M.S. Swaminathan**, often referred to as the "Father of the Green Revolution in India."
 
• States like **Punjab, Haryana, and Uttar Pradesh** were the major beneficiaries.
 
 
 
• **Limitations of Organic Compost:**
 
 
• While organic compost is beneficial for soil health, it lacks the high nutrient concentration required for HYV seeds to achieve their potential yields.
 
• Organic compost provides nutrients slowly over time, which is insufficient for the intensive needs of high-yield crops.
 
• It is not a substitute for chemical fertilisers in large-scale agriculture.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Forest Cover:**

 
 
• Forest cover helps in maintaining ecological balance, but it does not provide the nutrients required for HYV seeds.
 
• It plays a role in water conservation and climate regulation but is unrelated to the Green Revolution’s technological advancements.
 
 
 
• **Hand Tools:**
 
 
• Traditional hand tools were inadequate for large-scale farming during the Green Revolution.
 
• Modern machinery like tractors and harvesters replaced hand tools for efficient farm management.
 
 
 
• **Impact of the Green Revolution:**
 
 
• India achieved self-sufficiency in food grains, reducing dependence on imports.
 
• It led to socio-economic changes, including improved incomes for farmers and reduced poverty in rural areas.
 
• However, it also caused environmental concerns such as soil degradation, water pollution, and overuse of chemical fertilisers.

questions.question: Which country took over the Chairmanship of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP) on 1 January 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Australia**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP)** is a free trade agreement comprising 11 countries across the Asia-Pacific region.
 
• On **1 January 2025**, **Australia** took over the **Chairmanship** of the CPTPP, succeeding the previous Chair.
 
• The chairing role in the CPTPP is significant as it involves the coordination of meetings, ensuring the implementation of agreements, and facilitating discussions on new members or amendments.
 
• **Australia's Chairmanship** reflects its strong commitment to promoting free trade and economic integration in the Asia-Pacific region.
 
• The CPTPP aims to reduce trade barriers, promote fair competition, and establish a modern framework for international trade, which aligns with **Australia's economic interests**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership (CPTPP):**

 
 
• The CPTPP is an ambitious trade agreement signed on **8 March 2018**, involving 11 member countries: Australia, Canada, Japan, Mexico, New Zealand, Singapore, Vietnam, Peru, Malaysia, Chile, and Brunei.
 
• It was formed after the withdrawal of the United States from the original Trans-Pacific Partnership (TPP) in **2017**.
 
• The agreement covers a wide range of areas, including **trade in goods and services, intellectual property, labor standards, and environmental regulations**.
 
• The CPTPP represents approximately **13.4% of the global economy**, making it one of the largest free trade agreements in the world.
 
 
 
• **Australia’s Role:**
 
 
• Australia is a founding member of the CPTPP and has actively participated in its negotiations and implementation.
 
• As Chair, Australia will play a pivotal role in managing the strategic direction of the agreement and addressing challenges faced by member nations.
 
• Australia’s economy benefits significantly from the CPTPP through **enhanced market access for its goods and services**, particularly in the Asia-Pacific region.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of CPTPP:**
 
 
• The agreement eliminates **95% of tariffs** among member countries, promoting free trade and economic growth.
 
• It includes **provisions for labor rights, environmental protection, and intellectual property**, ensuring a balance between trade liberalization and social responsibility.
 
• The CPTPP promotes **digital trade** and e-commerce by reducing barriers and enhancing data flows across borders.
 
 
 
• **Potential New Members:**
 
 
• Several countries, including **the United Kingdom, South Korea, and China**, have expressed interest in joining the CPTPP, reflecting its growing significance in global trade.
 
• Australia, as Chair, will be responsible for facilitating discussions on the accession of new members and ensuring the integrity of the agreement.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Leadership Rotation:**

 
 
• The Chairmanship of the CPTPP rotates among member countries, allowing each nation to play an active role in shaping the agreement’s agenda.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance:**
 
 
• The CPTPP promotes economic integration, increases trade volumes, and strengthens supply chains among member countries.
 
• It is particularly beneficial for small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) due to reduced trade barriers and simplified customs procedures.
 
 
 
• **Impact on Global Trade:**
 
 
• The CPTPP is seen as a counterbalance to other major trade agreements, such as the **Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCEP)** and the **European Union’s trade initiatives**.
 
• It enhances the strategic influence of member countries in global trade negotiations.

questions.question: Who was the Chief Architect behind the integration of over 560 princely states into the Indian Union?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel**, also known as the "Iron Man of India," played a pivotal role in the integration of over **560 princely states** into the Indian Union after Independence in **1947**.
 
• Patel served as the first **Deputy Prime Minister** and **Home Minister** of India and utilized his diplomatic skills and authority to persuade princely states to join the Indian Union.
 
• He implemented the strategy of signing the **Instrument of Accession**, ensuring that the states would cede their control over defense, foreign affairs, and communications to the Indian government.
 
• Patel was supported by **V.P. Menon**, the Secretary of the States Department, in devising and implementing the plans for integration.
 
• Through a mix of diplomacy, negotiation, and in some cases military intervention (e.g., **Hyderabad**), Patel ensured the complete territorial integrity of India.** This historic achievement earned him the title of the "Unifier of India."**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sardar Vallabhbhai Patel:**

 
 
• Born on **31 October 1875** in **Nadiad, Gujarat**, he was a prominent leader of the Indian National Congress and played a crucial role in India's freedom struggle.
 
• He was posthumously awarded the **Bharat Ratna**, India’s highest civilian honor, in **1991**.
 
• His statue, known as the **Statue of Unity**, was unveiled in **2018** in Gujarat and is the **world’s tallest statue**.
 
 
 
• **Integration of Princely States:**
 
 
• India had **562 princely states** at the time of Independence, governed by local rulers who were given the choice to join India, Pakistan, or remain independent.
 
• States like **Hyderabad, Junagadh, and Kashmir** posed challenges, but Patel’s strategic interventions ensured their eventual accession.
 
• The **Indian Constitution** later recognized their territories as part of India.
 
 
 
• **Instrument of Accession:**
 
 
• This legal document was designed for the princely states to transfer control over their defense, foreign affairs, and communications to the Indian government.
 
• It was a crucial tool that facilitated the peaceful integration of most states.
 
 
 
• **Lord Mountbatten:**
 
 
• As the last Viceroy of India, he supported Patel’s efforts and played a guiding role in ensuring peaceful negotiations with princely states.
 
• However, his role was limited compared to Patel, who executed the integration process.
 
 
 
• **Challenges During Integration:**
 
 
• States like **Hyderabad** and **Junagadh** resisted joining India, leading to military interventions such as **Operation Polo** in Hyderabad.
 
• Kashmir’s accession involved complexities due to the tribal invasion and required military assistance.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legacy of Integration:**

 
 
• The integration of princely states laid the foundation for a unified and sovereign India.
 
• It reinforced the principle of national unity and territorial integrity, which continues to be a cornerstone of India's governance.
 
 
 
• **Other Contributors:**
 
 
• Although Patel was the chief architect, leaders like **Jawaharlal Nehru** and **Rajendra Prasad** also contributed to nation-building in different capacities.
 
• The collaboration between Patel and V.P. Menon was instrumental in achieving this monumental task.
 
 
 
• **Impact:**
 
 
• The successful integration ensured the political stability of post-Independence India, paving the way for economic and administrative reforms.
 
• This achievement remains one of the greatest feats in modern Indian history.
